title: First time i was impressed with a AI animation (GPT Astra 6.2)
author: AC-Daniel
selftext:
So far - AI wasnt able to animate these little sceletons in my game Necrolord. Thus, i made the "before" animatins by hand. Still better than anything what AI gave me - though not great at all. But now.... i think the difference is quite crazy. (ChatGPT Astra 6.2 - with codex)

If you want, you can watch those sceletons in game in my free demo => [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5282860/Necrolord/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5282860/Necrolord/)

comments.author: DVCL261804
comments.body: Love seeing a proper before and after like this, the skeletons in Necrolord look great. How did you actually get it to animate them, did you give it the sprite sheet and ask for new frames, or did it write code to rig and move the parts? Also curious if the frames needed much cleaning up by hand afterwards.

replies.author: AC-Daniel
replies.body: Nono, i dont work with a spritesheet since i have equipable weapons and in game, enemies can be cut appart. I have set up prefabs in unity consisting of about \~20 cutouts. Up till niow i animated everything by hand (just using unities standard tools) - but i got lots of critism especially for the walk animations. So i just said lets try out astra 6.2 - so far no model could do better then what i was able to do. I gave it some prompt help like => it used to look like an icescater, and you can insert additional cuts if needed. With those informations it created the new animations - though it burned a lot of tokens. So since i got a lo of creatues i will keep the hand made animations for most of it (as of now).  And no - i did not have to do any cleaning - i got it exactly like that. (if you mean by cleaning , like cleaning up the cutouts, i did this before with my old walking animations => this step also by hand as AI also really struggles with inpainting)

replies.author: AC-Daniel
replies.body: sorry and in regard to your other question about rigging. So my workflow is - design an image in idle pose, iterate over it until it fits the style and does not pop in comparision to other creatures. (Many say it looks super AI ... but i dont know... for me it looks like Heroes of might and magic 3 crossed with darkest dungeon what i wanted to achieve somehow). Then i by hand cutout the bodyparts in a graphic program GIMP (AI really struggles with it). In early stages of the game i then imported the cutouts piece by piece into unity and assembled a prefab. Now since AI knows what i want i taught it to just take in my GIMP files and build the prefab itself (did this way too late - wasted so much time :D ) ...Then, I have a prefab with sorting layers. I place them all in an idle pose and sorting layer defines what you see closest to the camera. The prefab is hierarchical - so if i move the shoulder, the whole arm moves, if i move the hand only the weapon+hand moves etc. => the workflow requires to clean up the individual cutouts and inpaint parts you dont see in the initial idle pose. I usually do this myself, since AI is really bad with it.

replies.author: DVCL261804
replies.body: Thanks for taking the time to write all that out, really useful. I can definitely see the Heroes 3 meets Darkest Dungeon look, especially in the Berserker. Getting the AI to build the prefab straight from your GIMP files is a clever shortcut, I can imagine how much time that saves now. Good luck with Necrolord!

comments.author: yunghollow69
comments.body:
Sorry but these are terrible. I clicked on one AI thread too many and now my regular reddit page shows me subs like this and I regularly see threads like these and I dont want to offend anyone, but do yall have eyes? I dont know enough about AI to say if there isnt a pipeline one could do that makes it look servicable, but this isnt it. If I can give yall one tip: if you insist of doing the art by AI and you just cant get it right, reduce the complexity, change the artstyle. From what Ive seen there are some things AI can actually generate that looks okay - although very easy to identify. But this kind of 2d art it just cant do yet.

If you want to really use that animation, used it on a sneaky enemy. Because those skeletons arent marching forward, they are tip-toeing.
